Next Session gives change-unknown three Problems across both structures and a mix of wholes; two or three clean first tries move this toward refuted, two or more assisted items move it to supported.

Works teen numbers in both directions, from 11 all the way to 19, including 10 + 7 and 10 + ? = 17.
Crosses ten in most cases, including doubles such as 8 + 8 and unequal pairs such as 3 + 9 and 9 + 3.
Counts on from the larger number even when the small number is said first, as in 1 + 7 and 2 + 11.
Handles subtraction and missing addends with both small and larger wholes, such as 6 - 1 and 12 + ? = 15.
Answered story Problems about totals and about what is left right away, as in 10 + 3, 9 - 2 and 9 + 3.
Worked out how many came or went away in stories such as 5 + ? = 9, 4 - ? = 3 and 5 - ? = 3.
Starts a Session strongly, with the first several Problems answered on the first try.
Uses a Hint well: after one nudge the change-unknown answers come out right.

practice.name: Counting on from the larger number

hypotheses.claim: Teen-number decompose items (10 + ? = teen) are less secure than compose items. Still refuted: the one teen item this Session, decompose 10 + ? = 18, was first-try correct and the fastest item of the Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep one compose and one decompose teen item present; help falling only on decompose items for two Sessions would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Partners to 10 is solid in both directions, including missing-partner items. Still proposed: only one partners item appeared this Session, take-from-ten 10 - 7, and it was first-try correct, so the two-item test was not run.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give two partners items, one of each structure; two first-try correct answers return this to supported, a Hint or Reveal on either keeps it proposed.

hypotheses.claim: The closing Problem of a Session is where performance drops. Still proposed and slightly stronger: for a fourth Session in a row the final item was helped (make-a-ten 6 + 7 at position 9, Hint-assisted), though help also fell at positions 2 and 5.
hypotheses.nextTest: Watch the final position again; a helped closing item with the rest of the Session clean moves this to supported, a clean closing item moves it toward refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Misses land on particular number combinations rather than on a whole structure. Still proposed and weak: none of the previously helped pairs were repeated exactly, but the teen counting-on shape that drew a Hint last Session (15 + 2) drew a Reveal again this Session in the form 2 + 14.
hypotheses.nextTest: Repeat the exact pairs that drew help (2 + 14, 8 - 2, 6 + 7) alongside untouched neighbours; help returning to those same pairs moves this to supported, clean repeats refute it.

hypotheses.claim: Within partners to 10, items with a large given number or a large amount taken away are less settled. Weakened: the only partners item this Session took away a large part (10 - 7) and was first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Offer one partners item with a given partner of 8 or 9 alongside one with a given partner of 1 to 3; help confined to the large-given item moves this to supported, help on the small-given item refutes it.

hypotheses.claim: Help tends to fall in the second half of a Session while the first half stays clean. Still refuted, though this Session was closer: help fell at positions 2, 5 and 9 of nine.
hypotheses.nextTest: Position is not being used as a lever; two consecutive Sessions with a clean first half and all help late would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Counting on holds when the larger addend is a single digit but not when it is in the teens. Supported: this Session both counting-on configurations appeared and the split was clean - 9 + 1 (single-digit larger addend) was first-try correct while 2 + 14 (teen larger addend) was a first-try miss ending in a Reveal, echoing the helped teen item 15 + 2 last Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give one single-digit and one teen counting-on item again; a second clean split keeps this supported, a clean teen item or help on the single-digit item weakens it.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on help is not tied to the size of the larger addend or to the order of the addends; it appears across configurations. Refuted: for a second Session running, the helped counting-on item had a teen larger addend (15 + 2, then 2 + 14 with a Reveal) while the single-digit item 9 + 1 was first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep both single-digit and teen counting-on items present; help scattered across both sizes for two Sessions would reopen this as proposed against h7.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten is the least settled Skill. Still proposed: the single make-a-ten item this Session (6 + 7) was a first-try miss ending in a Hint-assisted success, but result-unknown and counting-on also drew help, so it was not the only weak spot.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep two make-a-ten items across both orders; help returning only here restores supported, two clean items move it to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, help clusters on items containing a 7. Still refuted, with one counter-point: the only make-a-ten item this Session, 6 + 7, contained a 7 and drew a Hint, but 7 + 8 and 7 + 7 were clean last Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep 7-items and non-7 items both present in make-a-ten; help confined to 7-items for two Sessions would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: On missed items the Learner goes to a Reveal rather than working through a Hint. Still refuted: of three helped items this Session, two ended in Hint-assisted successes (8 - 2, 6 + 7) and one was a Reveal (2 + 14).
hypotheses.nextTest: Watch the mix again; two Sessions with Reveals outnumbering Hint-assisted successes would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, the missing-addend written form (a + ? = whole) draws help while the subtract form does not. Still refuted: the one unknown-addend item this Session was missing-addend (9 + ? = 14) and was first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep both unknown-addend forms present; help falling only on missing-addend items for two Sessions would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on items where the amount counted on is 1 have drawn more help than items counting on 2 or 3. Still refuted: 9 + 1 counted on 1 and was first-try correct, while the helped item counted on 2 (2 + 14).
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep plus-one items appearing in counting-on; two Sessions with help confined to plus-one items would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Help is confined to the unknown-addend Skill. Still refuted: the unknown-addend item was first-try correct while result-unknown, counting-on and make-a-ten all drew help.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep all Skills present; several Sessions with help falling only on unknown-addend would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Help on missing-addend items is not tied to the size of the whole. Still proposed: the missing-addend whole this Session was 14 with a missing part of 5, and it was first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give missing-addend items with wholes under 10 and wholes of 16-20; help appearing at both ends supports this, help confined to large wholes refutes it in favour of a size-based claim.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, difficulty tracks how large the part being removed or counted is rather than the written form. Still refuted: the missing part this Session was the largest allowed (5, in 9 + ? = 14) and the item was first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep offering unknown-addend items with large removed parts; two Sessions with help confined to those items would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: At the current mix of number sizes the Learner works without help across every unlocked Skill. Still refuted: three of nine items this Session needed help, across three Skills.
hypotheses.nextTest: Two consecutive fully clean Sessions at the top of the allowed ranges would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Within partners to 10, the take-from-ten form is currently less settled than the missing-partner form. Still refuted: the one take-from-ten item this Session (10 - 7) was first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep both partners structures present; two Sessions with help falling only on take-from-ten would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, help is not confined to one addend order. Supported: the helped make-a-ten item this Session was smaller-first (6 + 7, Hint-assisted), after earlier helped items in larger-first order.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep at least one make-a-ten item in each order; help again appearing in both orders keeps this supported, several Sessions of help in only one order refute it.

hypotheses.claim: First-try misses fall on Unit 2 crossing-ten work (make-a-ten and unknown-addend) while Unit 1 work (partners to 10, teen numbers) stays clean. Still refuted, but less clearly: Unit 1 items were clean (10 + ? = 18, 10 - 7) and make-a-ten drew a Hint, yet unknown-addend was clean and help also fell on counting-on and a Unit 3 result-unknown item.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep Unit 1 and Unit 2 Skills mixed; two consecutive Sessions with help falling only on Unit 2 crossing-ten items would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Help falls on items written with the blank in the middle (a + ? = total, including teen decompose) more than on items with the blank at the end. Still refuted, now in the opposite direction: both middle-blank items were clean (10 + ? = 18, 9 + ? = 14) and all three helped items had the blank at the end (8 - 2, 2 + 14, 6 + 7).
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep mixing middle-blank and end-blank items; two Sessions with help confined to middle-blank items would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Context only, not an ability claim: helped items have carried longer first-try times than clean ones. Supported again - the three helped items ran 4590 to 4899 ms while every first-try correct item ran 2211 to 3737 ms, with no overlap.
hypotheses.nextTest: Note the time bands again next Session; a helped item landing inside the clean range refutes this framing, which is bookkeeping only and never a reason to lower Mastery.

hypotheses.claim: Reveals land on items where the answer is a small remainder after ten is in view while items with larger answers stay clean. Still refuted: the only Reveal this Session was counting-on 2 + 14, with an answer of 16 and no ten being made.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep both small-answer and large-answer crossing-ten items present; two Sessions with Reveals confined to small answers would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, the largest sums draw help while smaller crossings stay clean. Still refuted: the helped make-a-ten item this Session was the smallest crossing offered (6 + 7), while 9 + 9 was clean last Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep make-a-ten items with larger addend 9 alongside 6s and 7s; two Sessions with help confined to the 9-items would reopen this as proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Result-unknown story problems will be handled on the first try at the small end of the range. Reopened as proposed: two of three small result-unknown items this Session were first-try correct (2 + 3, 1 + 3) while take-from 8 - 2 was a first-try miss ending in a Hint-assisted success.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give three small result-unknown items spread across add-to, take-from and put-together; all first-try correct moves this to supported, further help keeps it proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Difficulty on the Unit 3 result-unknown items comes from how the Problem is presented rather than from the size of the numbers. Supported: this Session 8 - 2 drew a Hint while the smaller add-to items 2 + 3 and 1 + 3 were first-try correct, and last Session 3 + 4 drew a Reveal while much larger crossing-ten items were clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give result-unknown items of similar small size across all three structures; help tracking structure rather than size keeps this supported, help tracking size refutes it.

hypotheses.claim: Help falls on items where the unknown or the amount joined or removed is only 1 or 2. Still proposed and mixed: 8 - 2 and 2 + 14 both had a change of 2 and drew help, but 9 + 1 (change of 1) and 1 + 3 were first-try correct while 9 + ? = 14 with a missing part of 5 was also clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Mix items whose change or unknown is 1 or 2 with items whose change is 3 to 5 across result-unknown, change-unknown and counting-on; help confined to the 1-or-2 items moves this to supported, help on a larger-change item refutes it.

hypotheses.claim: Within result-unknown, take-from items draw help while add-to items are answered on the first try: 8 - 2 was a first-try miss ending in a Hint-assisted success while 2 + 3 and 1 + 3 were first-try correct in the same Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give at least one take-from, one add-to and one put-together result-unknown item at similar sizes; help confined to take-from moves this to supported, a clean take-from item or help on add-to refutes it.

strengths: Adds and subtracts within small totals quickly and accurately: 2 + 3, 1 + 3 and 10 - 7 were all first-try correct.
Reads subtraction as an unknown addend, including missing parts as large as 5 with teen wholes (9 + ? = 14).
Takes teen decompose items in stride - 10 + ? = 18 was the fastest answer of the Session.
Uses Hints well: two of the three helped items ended in a correct answer after a Hint.
Keeps working after a Reveal and answers the following items correctly on the first try.
